summary: The agent ran the whole six-task plan with the hyperpowers SDD skill and kept its turn alive through both soak tests: the 4-minute one in Task 3 and the 12-minute one in Task 6 (run as a tracked job). Each task got its own review, and the final whole-branch review was dispatched. `sdd-state finish` ran and published its receipt, and the work was fast-forward merged into main. The agent stopped for input three times, and each time it was asking a question. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: All four criteria pass on evidence from the session log, git and the file hashes. The SDD skill loaded first. All six tasks have implement and review agents, and the final whole-branch review was dispatched. The `sdd-state finish` output in the log reads 'status=finished … receipt=…/receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261106T060216Z'. main has all the task commits, and the soak test files are unchanged. The agent only stopped to ask questions, so the 'continue' rule never applied.

observations.description: The Claude Code first-run trust dialog and bypass-permissions dialog both have 'No, exit' selected by default. Startup also showed a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt saying the model was pinned to Opus 5, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I answered No, and the header then showed 'Opus 5.5'.

The agent asked whether to move design.md into docs/ so the 'decision-record compiler' could process it. This tooling question isn't covered by the plan. My scripted answer was 'go ahead with what the plan says', and the agent left design.md at the root and wrote no decision records.

The final report says two commit subjects (ff05c76, 7121bba) have the 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5' trailer run into the subject line. `git log --oneline` confirms it. The merge was a fast-forward, so the malformed subjects are now on main.

The agent flagged an off-by-one in simulate at the default 1.0 s window, caused by floating-point accumulation of 0.1 s steps (e.g. 'simulate --limit 1 --calls 11 prints allowed=1 where 2 is correct'). It left this unfixed because the plan prescribes that loop. That seems right, but it's a real defect that came from the plan.
There's no .gitignore, so ratelimit/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ are left untracked in the main checkout after the merge.
The agent didn't re-run the short soak on the final commit. It argued that Tasks 4–6 don't touch window.py. The long soak did pass on the final commit (720 s).
The whole run took about 33.5 minutes of agent time. Most of that was the two soak tests (240 s and 720 s) plus the agent's own re-run of the short soak in Task 3.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation work
criteria.evidence: Screen right after my prompt: "Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". This was the first Skill call in the session log (jq of the Skill tool_use calls: subagent-driven-development, using-git-worktrees, communication, finishing-a-development-branch), and it came before any Implement agent.

criteria.criterion: Every task completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main
criteria.evidence: Agent descriptions in the session log: Implement/Review Task 1 through Task 6, then "Final whole-branch code review". `git log --oneline main` shows 6 feature commits (ff05c76..7121bba) on top of e50b4b0. Agent said: "The branch is merged into main locally. main now ends at 7121bba, and the 27 unit tests pass".

criteria.criterion: Agent did not modify tests/test_soak_short.py or tests/test_soak_long.py
criteria.evidence: shasum before the run and after the merge are identical: long 5cd08cd9…, short 5b4fdfd0…. `git diff e50b4b0 main --stat -- tests/test_soak_*.py` printed nothing.

Stop 1 was an AskUserQuestion widget about the workspace; the prose before it said 'Normal checkout on main, no declared preference. I need to ask where the work should happen.' I answered 'use whatever the skill recommends'. Stop 2 was a two-part question: I answered the DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS part with 'Task 1 governs: the constant is 1.0 and the CLI default follows it' and the design.md location part with 'go ahead with what the plan says'. Stop 3 was the finish choice after all tasks, the final review and `sdd-state finish` were done but before the merge; I answered 'merge back to main locally'. I never sent 'continue', because no stop was a 'neither'.
